articles.headline: Three Common Midlife Risk Factors Could Cost You 13 Years of Clear Memory
articles.body: New research tracked nearly 12,500 adults over 26 years and found that having hypertension, diabetes, or smoking at midlife dramatically cuts the number of years you live cognitively sharp. People with all three factors averaged just 17.5 dementia-free years after 55, compared to 30.1 years for those with none. The good news? It's cumulative, meaning controlling even one or two factors right now directly extends your mental clarity decades down the line.
articles.takeaway: Control your blood pressure, blood sugar, and quit smoking now. It's the difference between 17 and 30 more years of thinking clearly.
articles.source: Neurology Open Access (University of North Carolina)

articles.topic: Speed training brain cognitive decline prevention
articles.headline: Ten Minutes a Day of Brain Games Just Delayed Dementia by Years
articles.body: A landmark 20-year study followed 2,000+ adults and found that specific cognitive speed training—done for just weeks decades earlier—cut dementia diagnoses in half. The training involved quick visual recognition tasks that get progressively harder. Even more striking: benefits held strong when researchers checked medical records in 2019, when many participants were in their 90s. Speed training seems to build stronger neural networks that protect thinking ability long-term.
articles.takeaway: Quick-reflex brain training beats memory games. Just a few weeks of practice can pay cognitive dividends for 20 years.
articles.source: Alzheimer's & Dementia: Translational Research and Clinical Interventions

articles.topic: Daily routine circadian rhythm pain depression
articles.headline: Same Wake Time Every Day Just Beat Your Pain and Sadness. Even With Insomnia.
articles.body: University of Missouri researchers studied 67 older adults and found something simple but powerful: people who kept consistent daily schedules—same bedtime, meal times, and activities—had significantly less physical pain and depression. Remarkably, this held true even for those struggling with insomnia. The mechanism? Regular timing signals sync your circadian rhythm, the 24-hour internal clock that controls inflammation, mood, and pain perception. Routine is literally medicine.
articles.takeaway: Stick to the same wake and sleep times, even weekends. Consistency beats sleep quality for managing pain and mood.

articles.topic: Fruit juice smoothie depression mood mental health
articles.headline: One Glass a Day Just Lowered Depression Scores in Four Weeks
articles.body: Newcastle University researchers ran a randomized trial with adults who normally ate little fruit. After four weeks, those who added just one daily glass of 100% fruit juice or a smoothie to their diet reported measurably lower depression scores compared to a control group. Both groups increased overall fruit intake, but the juice group saw the mood lift. The effect was modest but statistically significant, and no negative metabolic changes appeared. Sometimes the simplest moves move your mental health.
articles.takeaway: Add one glass of juice or smoothie daily when boosting produce intake. The mood boost is real and happens fast.

workout.title: Dead Hang, Row, and Hollow: Back and Core in 30
equipment: pull-up bar or sturdy doorframe bar
workout.tip: If you don't have a pull-up bar, substitute the dead hangs and rows with resistance band pull-aparts and band rows anchored in a doorframe. Quality over quantity every set.
workout.warmup: Spend 3 minutes on arm circles, shoulder rolls, and cat-cow spinal waves. Then do 10 scapular shrugs in a relaxed hang or with arms overhead to wake up the muscles around your shoulder blades before pulling anything heavy.

exercises.name: Dead Hang
exercises.notes: Grip a bar with both hands, hang fully with shoulders packed down away from ears — do not let them shrug up. Breathe steadily. If grip fails early, use a resistance band looped around the bar for support.

exercises.name: Inverted Row (using a table edge or low bar)
exercises.notes: Lie under a sturdy table or low bar, grip overhand, and pull your chest up to meet it. Keep your body in a rigid plank line — no hips sagging. The lower you position your body, the harder it gets.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart
exercises.notes: Hold a resistance band at chest height with arms extended in front of you. Pull both ends apart until your arms are wide, squeezing the back of your shoulders together. Control the return — do not let the band snap back.

exercises.name: Superman Hold
exercises.notes: Lie face down, arms extended overhead. Lift arms, chest, and legs off the floor simultaneously and hold for 3 counts. This works the posterior chain and lower back without any equipment at all.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Lie on your back, press your lower back into the floor, extend arms overhead and legs out low. Hold the position while breathing normally. If your back lifts off the floor, raise your legs higher until you can maintain contact.

workout.cooldown: Finish with a 90-second doorframe chest stretch on each side and a slow child's pose hold for 60 seconds to decompress the spine and let the back muscles relax after pulling work.

If grip fails early, use a resistance band looped around the bar for support. Inverted Row (using a table edge or low bar): 3 sets x 10-12 — Lie under a sturdy table or low bar, grip overhand, and pull your chest up to meet it. Keep your body in a rigid plank line — no hips sagging. The lower you position your body, the harder it gets. Band Pull-Apart: 3 sets x 15 — Hold a resistance band at chest height with arms extended in front of you. Pull both ends apart until your arms are wide, squeezing the back of your shoulders together. Control the return — do not let the band snap back. Superman Hold: 3 sets x 8, hold 3 seconds each — Lie face down, arms extended overhead. Lift arms, chest, and legs off the floor simultaneously and hold for 3 counts. This works the posterior chain and lower back without any equipment at all. Hollow Body Hold: 3 sets x 20-30 seconds — Lie on your back, press your lower back into the floor, extend arms overhead and legs out low. Hold the position while breathing normally. If your back lifts off the floor, raise your legs higher until you can maintain contact. meal.title: Seared Tuna and Farro Bowl with Avocado and Lemon Herb Dressing
meal.description: Cook farro in bulk on Sunday and refrigerate. This bowl comes together in under 10 minutes when the grain is already done.
meal.instructions:
Ingredients:
2 x 5 oz tuna steaks
1 cup cooked farro
1 ripe avocado, sliced
2 cups baby spinach
1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
2 tbsp olive oil
Juice of 1 lemon
1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
1 tsp Dijon mustard
Salt, black pepper, and chili flakes to taste

Instructions:
1. Season tuna steaks with salt, pepper, and chili flakes. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a pan over high heat and sear tuna for 90 seconds per side. Remove and slice. 2. Whisk remaining olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, parsley, salt, and pepper into a dressing. 3. Build bowls with farro as the base, then spinach, cherry tomatoes, and avocado. 4. Lay sliced tuna on top and drizzle with lemon herb dressing.
